subject: Our World and Our People
name: KG1 Our World and Our People
description: The KG1 curriculum integrates Language & Literacy, Numeracy, Creative Arts, and Our World and Our People into thematic strands to provide holistic learning experiences.

strands.title: ALL ABOUT ME
strands.description: Learners explore their unique identity, body parts, personal hygiene, healthy living, environmental health, and personal safety.

subStrands.title: I am a wonderful and Unique creation
subStrands.description: Understanding self-identity and unique bodily features.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the understanding that all learners are wonderful and have unique body features that make them different from other people and other God's creation in the environment.

indicators.description: Identify and talk in simple sentences, about the features of our body that make us unique and different from other God's creation. E.g. animals.

exemplars.description: With learners seated in a big circle outside the classroom, and using "pass a ball" game, learners take turns to use positive language to describe and appreciate themselves.

indicators.description: Sing an action song that helps learners name the parts of the body and point to them.

exemplars.description: Have learners sing different songs in their local language and/or in the English language that identify parts of the body and perform actions on it. E.g. Head, shoulders knees and toes.

indicators.description: Recognize and talk about the different parts of book, (the front/ cover page of a book and back of a book) and relate the content of the text to our body parts.

exemplars.description: As part of the process of the daily read aloud lesson, have learners talk about the front/cover and the back page of a book, and ask them to make connections to their own body.

indicators.description: Use new and positive expressions/vocabulary related to the parts of the body.

exemplars.description: Have learners watch a displayed conversational poster on the wall (parts of the human body) and use the positive descriptive words and expression they learnt to describe themselves.

indicators.description: Sing songs about the body parts and the letters of the alphabet and clap hands on the rhythm of the songs.

exemplars.description: Have learners sit in a semi-circle, using pictures and toys, let pupils identify the different parts of their body.

indicators.description: Draw a beautiful picture of themselves and scribble freely underneath the picture paper.

exemplars.description: Learners are asked to draw themselves, colour it nicely, after which they scribble freely underneath.

indicators.description: Create sets of human parts that are similar and represent them with numbers up to 5.

exemplars.description: In pairs, the learners check on the body parts that are similar and draw them in Sets, count them and represent them with numbers one to five (1-5).

subStrands.title: The parts of the human body and their functions
subStrands.description: Identifying body parts and their specific functions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the understanding of appropriate names of the parts of the body and describe the functions of each part.

indicators.description: Using a conversation poster of body parts, learners talk about the functions of the parts of the human body that we can see.

exemplars.description: Have learners sing the song about the body parts and what they do. Perform activities like blindfolding to identify functions.

indicators.description: Use visual information to aid comprehension before, during and after reading a text on functions of the parts of the human body.

exemplars.description: Guide learners to demonstrate how books are read from left to right. Have learners think critically about illustrations in the Big book on body parts.

indicators.description: Learn and use new /vocabulary related to what they do with the parts of the body.

exemplars.description: Have learners use different parts of the body to perform different actions and use new words learnt to describe what they are doing.

indicators.description: Count the number of the names of the body parts in songs through clapping on the rhythm.

exemplars.description: Learners sing songs, clap on the rhythm and count the number of parts they hear.

indicators.description: Sing songs about functions of the body parts and perform the actions on it.

exemplars.description: Have learners sing songs related to functions of the body parts and perform actions on it. Call the body part and have learners perform what they use it for.

indicators.description: Colour an outline of a part of the body used in performing a function.

exemplars.description: Display an outline of drawing on a paper for pupils to colour and tell what the illustration is about to friends.

indicators.description: Compare lines and other shapes that are same and different.

exemplars.description: Through think-pair-share, have learners compare lines and shape of their body parts (e.g. head looks like a circle, arms are straight).

subStrands.title: Caring for the parts of my body
subStrands.description: Personal hygiene and care for body parts.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the importance of personal hygiene and how to care for my body parts.

indicators.description: Sing songs and recite rhymes about how we take care of each part of the body and demonstrate how to do it.

exemplars.description: Have learners sit in a semi-circle and sing a song like 'This is the way I brush my teeth' and call out parts of the body to care for.

indicators.description: Watch a short video clip and talk about how to care for the various parts of the body.

exemplars.description: Show a video clip on correct ways to care for body parts. Guide learners to count materials used to clean the body.

indicators.description: Talk about what we use in caring for the human body in our everyday life as they listen to a read aloud text.

exemplars.description: Have learners listen to a Big Book read aloud and demonstrate how to care for different parts of the body.

indicators.description: Show and explain why learners' books are open from left to right.

exemplars.description: Do a picture walk through a book and have learners identify the direction of reading (left to right).

indicators.description: Stress the words that show caring for the body as learners sing songs about personal care.

exemplars.description: Have learners repeat songs about washing/brushing, clapping rhythm to stress care words.

indicators.description: Match the parts of the body to the tools we use in caring for the body and colour them with same colour.

exemplars.description: Display an outline of drawing for pupils to match tools (soap, brush) with body parts and colour them.

indicators.description: Use number names to count, find out how many and match body parts with other part with same number (1-5).

exemplars.description: Show picture of different parts put in a set (e.g. two eyes, one mouth) and model how to match.

indicators.description: Use number names to count, find out how many and match body parts with other part with same number (1-5)

exemplars.description: Show picture of different parts put in a set e.g. two eyes, one mouth, two hands, five fingers matched with 5 toes. Model how to match and have learners match them in their workbook.

subStrands.title: Keeping my Body healthy by eating good food and taking my vaccination

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the understanding that eating good food and taking all my childhood vaccinations will keep me growing healthy and strong.

indicators.description: Learners talk about different types of food they eat at home and classify those that can make them grow healthy.

exemplars.description: Learners discuss subtheme in community circle. Use conversational posters to identify balanced food groups (Fats, Protein, Carbohydrates, Calcium, Fruit/Veg, Whole Grain).

indicators.description: Tell their own short stories about pictures in the Big book to be read.

exemplars.description: Have learners talk about pictures in the book and make connections to written symbols.

indicators.description: Listen attentively, respond to an information text about foods we eat to keep healthy.

exemplars.description: Learners listen to teacher-read-aloud on balanced diet. Mention and discuss different food types. Count examples of foods identified.

indicators.description: Count and clap the keywords in songs about types of food.

exemplars.description: Model how to sing, clap, and count words in a song about food.

indicators.description: Sing Alphabet song about food and identify the beginning letter of common food items.

exemplars.description: Learners sing alphabet song and identify letters beginning food names (e.g. Banana begins with /b/).

indicators.description: Draw a picture of any food item that has its name beginning with the letter B.

exemplars.description: Teacher models writing the letter in the air. Learners practice and then draw a food item and write the letter.

indicators.description: Sort and classify different food items under the six food groups and into shapes.

exemplars.description: Classify food items into six food groups. Sort healthy food items into shapes.

indicators.description: Sing and dance to traditional songs about foods.

exemplars.description: Have learners sing traditional songs about food in locality and dance.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of how keeping our home and school environment clean can keep us healthy and strong.

indicators.description: Talk about how we can keep our environment clean in order to avoid getting sick.

exemplars.description: Use conversational poster regarding pollution/defecation. Discuss causes of sickness and how to keep environment clean.

indicators.description: Recognize that written symbols in books carry important information about the pictures.

exemplars.description: Do picture walk through Big book. Ask learners to tell story about pictures.

indicators.description: Listen attentively to the read aloud text and share what they have learnt about diseases from dirty environments.

exemplars.description: Use KWL strategy for reading informational book on diseases. Learners share what they learnt.

indicators.description: Compose their stories about pictures in the book to be read.

exemplars.description: Learners create stories about pictures before reading. Stress cleanliness words (neat, clean, tidy).

indicators.description: Sing alphabet songs that contain the letter of the week.

exemplars.description: Introduce letter of the week (e.g. 'a'). Write boldly. Introduce keyword related to disease/environment.

indicators.description: Begin to write letters of the alphabet.

exemplars.description: Learners exercise wrist/fingers. Model writing letter in air/sand/slate.

indicators.description: Prepare posters with pictures to post in the environment cautioning people.

exemplars.description: Provide materials for pupils to prepare posters writing 'NO' to mess/dirt. Post in school compound.

indicators.description: Describe the attributes of 3-D objects and draw them.

exemplars.description: Describe attributes of 3-D objects. Learners bring examples from nature walk.

subStrands.title: Protecting ourselves from home and road accidents

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of measures to take to keep safe (from accidents, hurts, and harms).

indicators.description: Talk about possible accidents we can have at home and at school and safety measures.

exemplars.description: Discuss possible home/road accidents. Role-play safety measures. Teach traffic light rhyme.

indicators.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language in books.

exemplars.description: Picture walk through Big book. Use LEA (Language Experience Approach) to write learners' dictated stories.

indicators.description: Listen to and respond to a read aloud text about keeping safe in the environment.

exemplars.description: Use KWL strategy. Read book on protection against harm/sharp objects. Practice safety measures.

indicators.description: Clap and count syllables in longer words.

exemplars.description: Introduce longer words (objects, strangers, electricity). Practice clapping and counting syllables.

indicators.description: Use vocabulary learnt to express and demonstrate how to protect themselves.

exemplars.description: In pairs, use words from read-aloud to teach each other safety. Use 'Show and tell' with drawn objects.

indicators.description: Describe the attributes of 3-D objects and sort objects into planes and 3-D objects.

exemplars.description: Revise 3-D attributes. Sort objects from home into planes and 3D objects.

indicators.description: Draw and colour five harmful objects that can cause accidents.

exemplars.description: Give learners outline of harmful objects to colour or draw their own (knife, fire, etc.).

strands.title: MY FAMILY
strands.description: Learners explore family types, family history, celebrations, and rules that guide school family life.

subStrands.title: Types and members of my Family

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the importance, roles and responsibilities of family members.

indicators.description: Discuss different types of family they have at home, their roles and responsibilities.

exemplars.description: In community circle, learners mention family members and roles. Discuss nuclear, single, extended families.

indicators.description: Demonstrate that print matches with illustration in a book.

exemplars.description: Identify key elements of book front matter. Use interactive reading to track text. Match illustration to print.

indicators.description: Listen, interact actively in a read aloud session on a story about families.

exemplars.description: Picture walk and prediction. Introduce vocabulary. Interactive reading about family members.

indicators.description: Identify the names and words with similar beginning sounds.

exemplars.description: Sing song about birth days. Mention names of family members. Identify names with similar initial sounds.

indicators.description: Talk about the basic concepts of writing: from left to right, and top to bottom.

exemplars.description: Warm up exercise. Introduce writing vertical straight-line strokes from top to down.

indicators.description: Introduce the concept 'more than' to learners and solve some word puzzles.

exemplars.description: Collect data on birth days. Represent with milk tins. Solve problems on 'Which group has more members?'.

indicators.description: Role-play the responsibilities of family members.

exemplars.description: Role play dad, mom, and other members. Highlight responsibilities.

subStrands.title: Origin and History of my Family

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the origin and history of our families.

indicators.description: Listen and tell stories about origin and history of their family members.

exemplars.description: Greet in home languages. Tell story of major tribes in the region.

indicators.description: Demonstrate that print matches with illustration in a book.

exemplars.description: Discuss front matter. Predict story. Track text. Count words in sentences.

indicators.description: Listen, interact actively in a read aloud session on a story about origin and history.

exemplars.description: Picture walk. Introduce vocabulary on languages/regions. Show Ghana map. Read story.

indicators.description: Identify the names and words with similar beginning sounds.

exemplars.description: Sing song about hometowns. Identify towns with similar initial sounds. Group and count.

indicators.description: Talk about the basic concepts of writing: write from left to right, and top to bottom.

exemplars.description: Warm up. Writing curves on a straight line. Draw heads of family members.

indicators.description: Use comparative language/phrases 'more than', 'less than', or 'same as'.

exemplars.description: Collect data on language groups. Represent with tins. Compare using comparative language.

indicators.description: Draw a family tree that includes Grandpa and Grandma.

exemplars.description: Draw family tree. Compare drawings. Count girls and boys.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the knowledge of celebrations and festivals that the individual families celebrate.

indicators.description: Talk about some special family days and activities e.g. birthdays, naming, festivals.

exemplars.description: Discuss conversational poster of festival. Talk about family celebrations. Sing songs.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the proper way to handle a book.

exemplars.description: Observe/practice holding book upright, opening cautiously. Count pages read.

indicators.description: Listen, interact actively in a read aloud session on a story about families.

exemplars.description: KWL strategy for read aloud on festivals. Explain vocabulary. Share learnings.

indicators.description: Talk about the basic concepts of writing: from left to right, and top to bottom.

exemplars.description: Warm up. Writing vertical straight-line strokes.

indicators.description: Use comparative language 'more than', 'less than', or 'same as' to show relation.

exemplars.description: Collect data on birth months. Compare groups using comparative language.

indicators.description: Create special birthday cards for loved ones using different writing and drawing tools.

exemplars.description: Design birthday cards. Classify cards.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the rules and regulations that governs the members of the school.

indicators.description: Talk about the members of the school, activities they do and create rules.

exemplars.description: Community Circle time to discuss school family members and activities. Create rules.

indicators.description: Demonstrate that print matches with illustration in a book.

exemplars.description: Predict content using cover. Interactive reading tracking text. Count words in sentences.

indicators.description: Use the vocabulary acquired in the read aloud session to prepare rules.

exemplars.description: Read text on school rules. Create classroom rules using pictures/colours.

indicators.description: Identify and look for more rhyming words in different rhymes related to school.

exemplars.description: Recite rhymes. Identify rhyming sounds. Group objects.

indicators.description: Recognize and identify the target letter name for the week in given words.

exemplars.description: Introduce letter (e.g. /s/). Show position in keywords. Practice writing.

indicators.description: Solve story problems using comparative language.

exemplars.description: Collect data on birth days. Solve 'less than' problems. Write signs.

strands.title: VALUES AND BELIEFS
strands.description: Learners develop family, cultural, religious, and moral values, and learn to relate well with people of different beliefs.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the good manners that our families values and why they value them.

indicators.description: identify the good manners our families value and how it can change our personal likes and dislikes.

exemplars.description: Discuss likes/dislikes. Discuss family values. Sort 'likes' from 'dislikes'. Teach song on good manners.

indicators.description: Demonstrate that spoken words are represented in written words/print

exemplars.description: Read Big Book pointing to words. Create version of story using LEA.

indicators.description: Listen to a story on importance of exhibiting good manners and role-play greetings.

exemplars.description: Discuss good manners. Tell Ananse story on greetings. Role play daily greetings.

indicators.description: Recognise that spoken words are made up of individual speech sounds and letters.

exemplars.description: Sing Alphabet song. Stretch words to count sounds. Phonics game replacing initial sounds.

indicators.description: Recognize details in shapes and height of the letter for the week and write it legibly.

exemplars.description: Model pre-writing. Write letter in air/sand/slate. Create simple patterns with shapes.

indicators.description: Show the time of the day using clock faces.

exemplars.description: Use clock to explain time of day. Practice manipulating clock faces.

indicators.description: Draw clock faces and write down the given time under it.

exemplars.description: Discuss importance of time. Draw clock faces showing different times.

subStrands.title: My Cultural Values
subStrands.description: Cultural values like respect and politeness.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of cultural values.

indicators.description: Talk about some important cultural values and good manners that promote respect and politeness

exemplars.description: Discuss polite words/greetings. Demonstrate showing respect. Role play scenarios.

indicators.description: Recognize the basic components of a book using the Big Book on Showing respect.

exemplars.description: Talk about book components. Predict content. Interactive read aloud. Fill in missing letters.

indicators.description: Use positive words learnt from the teacher-read-aloud to talk about how to show respect.

exemplars.description: Picture walk. Read aloud Big Book on respect. Dramatize ways to show respect. Count words in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify the location of individual sounds in a given word (beginning or end).

exemplars.description: Introduce target letter-sound. Search for words with sound at different positions. Practice writing.

indicators.description: Practice using the more than and less than concept and their signs to compare items.

exemplars.description: Talk about likes/dislikes. Enumerate behaviours. Use comparative language and signs.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the religious and moral values and virtues.

indicators.description: Recite rhymes and talk about religious values and how to show it

exemplars.description: Recite rhymes/sing songs on values. Discuss common moral values (love, forgiveness). Dramatize.

indicators.description: Handle books correctly and with care.

exemplars.description: Demonstrate handling books. Discuss effects of mishandling. Explain 2/3 D shapes using book.

indicators.description: Interact actively with peers during a teacher-read aloud session about religious and moral values.

exemplars.description: Interactive read aloud. Use visual information for keywords. Identify 2/3 D objects in illustrations.

indicators.description: stretch and count the number of sounds in a word and blend them together.

exemplars.description: Model stretching words. Sound blending games. Introduce silent letters.

indicators.description: Write letters legibly and boldly

exemplars.description: Prewriting exercises. Write words on values. Count letters. Create patterns.

indicators.description: Write numeral 1 to 5 and represent them with different objects.

exemplars.description: Count letters in words. Match words with number cards. Form patterns with shapes.

subStrands.title: Our Beliefs
subStrands.description: Understanding different beliefs and relating well with others.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of and relating well with people with different beliefs

indicators.description: Talk about God as the Creator of all things and discuss different ways that people worship him.

exemplars.description: KWL strategy on beliefs. Share knowledge about God/worship. Dramatize worship.

indicators.description: Handle their religious scriptures (book) appropriately.

exemplars.description: Display scriptures. Scaffold learners to identify how to open books. Sing/draw objects.

indicators.description: Interact actively with peers during a teacher-read aloud session about religious beliefs.

exemplars.description: Read informational text on religious groups. Role play leaders. Count letters in names of books.

indicators.description: Draw one activity that we do when worshipping God and label it.

exemplars.description: Discuss worship. Draw/paint/label worship activity. Sort drawings.

indicators.description: Play different musical instrument, sing religious songs and dance on the music.

exemplars.description: Perform religious songs/dance. Add numbers (money collection). Read/copy sight words.

strands.title: MY LOCAL COMMUNITY
strands.description: Learners identify special places, occupations, and leaders in their local community and understand their roles.

subStrands.title: Knowing the Special Places in My Local Community

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the special places in our local communities

indicators.description: Visit and talk about some special places in our community

exemplars.description: Identify special places from posters. Field trip. Draw special place. Group drawings.

indicators.description: Use visual information (illustrations) when reading.

exemplars.description: Picture walk. Read Big book on special places. 'Pick and Act' game for vocabulary.

indicators.description: Listen attentively and interact with peers during a teacher-read-aloud session about special places.

exemplars.description: Read Big book. Retell story. Group places visited. Represent numbers.

indicators.description: Find as many words in the community in which we can find the new letter-sound for the week.

exemplars.description: Teach tongue twister. Teach pronunciation/writing of letter. Search for words.

indicators.description: Colour nicely a scene from the community and label it.

exemplars.description: Draw/colour scene from community. Caption/label it.

indicators.description: Demonstrate their understanding of the concept of addition by combining people and objects.

exemplars.description: Create market scene. Combine money/items to find total.

subStrands.title: Knowing (who) the Important People/Occupation in My Community

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the people in the community and their occupation.

indicators.description: Talk about who the neighbours are, the work they do and how important their profession are.

exemplars.description: Community Circle time discussion on neighbours/occupations. Draw future uniform. Sort occupations.

indicators.description: Demonstrate that sentences are made of words and that words are separated in print.

exemplars.description: 'Be the word' game to demonstrate sentence structure/spacing.

indicators.description: Interact with resource people from different occupation

exemplars.description: Interact with resource people using KWL. Role play occupations.

indicators.description: Recognize the letter-sound learnt in the previous week in words

exemplars.description: Identify letter sound in words (game). Treasure hunt for words.

indicators.description: Write boldly and legibly the target letter for the week and add a name of a friend to it.

exemplars.description: Exercise fingers. Practice writing. Form sentences and count words.

indicators.description: Draw themselves in the uniform of their aspired future job, colour it nicely and write name.

exemplars.description: Draw/colour future job uniform. Group by profession and count.

indicators.description: Demonstrate their understanding of the concept of subtraction as separating and finding out how many is left.

exemplars.description: Market scene subtraction activities.

subStrands.title: Knowing the Special Leaders in My Community

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding and knowledge of the special leaders and their roles in our communities.

indicators.description: Talk about and describe the traditional and religious leaders in our community.

exemplars.description: Discuss religious/traditional leaders. Role play activities. Count leaders in Big book.

indicators.description: Listen attentively to an informational read aloud text on who our special leaders are.

exemplars.description: KWL strategy. Read text. Learners share learning.

indicators.description: Sing traditional songs, play rattle and shakers, clap and dance on the correct rhythm.

exemplars.description: Sing/play instruments/dance. Talk about experience.

indicators.description: Recognize and identify target letter name and the sound in items and names.

exemplars.description: Teach new letter sound. Practice writing. Identify in words.

indicators.description: Role play the various leaders and what they do in the community.

exemplars.description: Role play leaders at meeting. Create Adinkra symbols.

indicators.description: Demonstrate their understanding of the concept of subtraction as separating and finding out how many is left.

exemplars.description: Subtraction story problems (e.g. Chief donating books).

strands.title: MY NATION GHANA
strands.description: Learners explore Ghana’s independence, national identity, symbols, and celebrations.

subStrands.title: History and Celebration of Ghana's Independence

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the history and independence of Ghana

indicators.description: Locate their home regions on an outline map of Ghana and talk about the history behind their festivals.

exemplars.description: Use map of Ghana. Locate home regions. Tell history of festivals. Group/count/add/subtract cut-out papers.
Learners retell the story about Ghana's independence using KWL. Watch video. Role play 6th March.

indicators.description: Show peers that sentences are made of words and that words are separated in print.

exemplars.description: 'Be the word' game. Rearrange words to form sentences. Count letters for addition/subtraction.

indicators.description: Listen attentively and interact with peers during a teacher-read-aloud session about the Independence Day.

exemplars.description: Interactive read aloud. Use illustrations. Use vocabulary. Draw celebration scene. Addition/subtraction.

indicators.description: Demonstrate respect for the symbols and songs of our nation.

exemplars.description: Sing national anthem/recite pledge. Build collage of Ghana Flag.

indicators.description: Sing Alphabet song and point to the letters of the alphabet in the classroom.

exemplars.description: Sing alphabet songs. Make sentences. Subtraction of letters.

indicators.description: Create and perform dance movements and music inspired by Ghanaian history and other cultures

exemplars.description: Listen/dance to Ghanaian history music. Organize Kiddies march past.

indicators.description: Compose and decompose numbers up to ten

exemplars.description: Decompose 10 bottle tops. Use dot cards to decompose numbers.

strands.title: ALL AROUND US
strands.description: Learners explore living and non-living things, animals, water, air, plants, gardening, light, and changing weather conditions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of living and non-living things.

indicators.description: Talk about different types of things around us and classify them into living things and non-living things

exemplars.description: Recite poem. Nature walk. Discuss and classify things seen.

indicators.description: Participate actively in an Interactive Read Aloud story about living and non-living things

exemplars.description: Pre-reading activities. Interactive reading. Post-reading summary. Draw living/non-living things.

indicators.description: Blend letter sounds to form words related to the theme.

exemplars.description: Identify letter sounds. Clap syllables. Blend sounds.

indicators.description: Identify and write initial sounds of the objects.

exemplars.description: Identify living/non-living things. Identify/match initial sounds.

indicators.description: Identify and describe objects by colour names and size

exemplars.description: Use conversational posters. Describe by colour/size. Create patterns.

indicators.description: Recognise, sort, classify, describe and extend non numerical patterns.

exemplars.description: Recognise/describe simple repeating patterns (sound, shape, colour). Extend patterns.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of domestic and wild animals.

indicators.description: Sing and talk about different kinds of animals, what they eat, the sound they make and put them into groups.

exemplars.description: Recite poem. Discuss domestic animals/uses/sounds. Sort and count.

indicators.description: Handle a book correctly e.g. hold the book upright and open from left to right

exemplars.description: Pre-reading with Big book. Echo-reading. Highlight book handling.

indicators.description: Tap or clap and count the syllables of the names of animals and identify the initial sound.

exemplars.description: Sing song. Mimic sounds. Clap syllables. Create patterns with syllables.

indicators.description: Review list of letter sounds learnt and use letter sounds to list and match the pictures of animals.

exemplars.description: Recap letter sounds. List animals by initial sound. Sort picture cards.

indicators.description: Identify and describe objects by colour names and size.

exemplars.description: Describe animal features. Colour outline. Create patterns.

indicators.description: Recognise, sort, classify, describe and extend non numerical patterns.

exemplars.description: Recap pattern activities. Create patterns with sound/syllables.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of sources of water and its uses.

indicators.description: Talk about where we get water from and its uses.

exemplars.description: Sing rhymes. Discuss sources (rain, well, river etc.) and uses. Draw source.

indicators.description: Listen and interact with teacher and peers as they listen to a read aloud text on the uses.

exemplars.description: Pre-reading. Read information text. Post-reading activities. Sequence sources.

indicators.description: Recognise letter sounds and names which begin words that describe how human beings and animals use water.

exemplars.description: Identify initial/ending sounds of words (drinking, washing). Role play uses.

indicators.description: Use a variety of new vocabulary learnt about the sources of water to make simple sentences orally.

exemplars.description: Use keywords to make sentences. Identify position on word grid.

indicators.description: Design, make, exhibit, and respond to own or others art works.

exemplars.description: Make picture of water source. Label. Sort and arrange.

indicators.description: Describe the position of objects.

exemplars.description: Sequence items. Describe position (1st to 5th). Use number grid.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the presence of air and tell its importance.

indicators.description: Share their understanding and describe the presence of air through experimentation.

exemplars.description: Recite rhymes. Experiment with balloons, kites, running with cloth.

indicators.description: Use visual information to help them understand the text they read.

exemplars.description: Pre-reading prediction. Use picture clues. Count experiments read about.

indicators.description: Recognize the position of the target sounds in words either at the initial, middle or the ending.

exemplars.description: Identify position of target sound. Clap number of target sounds in words.

indicators.description: Use a variety of new vocabulary learnt about importance of air to make simple sentence orally.

exemplars.description: Pick and act words (breathing, cooling). Make sentences. Write position of letters.

indicators.description: Derive meaning and make judgment about artworks using the senses according to its beauty.

exemplars.description: Observe art work on air experiments. Demonstrate uses. LEA story.

indicators.description: Describe the position of objects.

exemplars.description: Line up pictures. Name positions.

subStrands.title: Plants - 1
subStrands.description: Introduction to parts of plants and their functions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the parts of plants and their functions.

indicators.description: Sing and talk about parts of a plants and their functions

exemplars.description: In a community circle time, let learners sing songs about plants and discuss the parts. Using a picture or a real plant, guide learners to point to and name the part (roots, stem, leaf/leaves). After detailed discussion have learners make sentences with the parts of plant e.g. this is the leaf, this is the roots. Post a drawn tree on the board, using word cards, have learners pick and post the card at the appropriate part. Repeat the activity to ensure that learners can identify the main parts of a tree. Using a poster or picture, have learners draw, colour and label a plant and talk about their drawing using the right terms/names.

indicators.description: Talk about the cover page of the book and point to individual words while listening to the teacher read aloud.

exemplars.description: As part of the pre-reading activities, show and talk about the cover page, let learners identify the colour and some letters written on the book e.g. title of the book, name of the writer, etc. Run a pointer under the words while reading, use questions to encourage learners talk about parts and usefulness of plants to human beings as they listen to a read aloud story on plants (the last tree dies the last man dies). In addition to the picture of trees in the book, display 3-D objects with varied attributes and have leaners touch and feel during the discussion. Guide learners describe the given 3-D objects according to a given attribute e.g. shape, size etc. with words/phrases/sentences like "round", "flat", "The book is flat", "A pencil rolls", "An eraser is smaller than a book"

indicators.description: Blend individual sounds and decode simple words which relates to the theme.

exemplars.description: Using the letter cards, guide learners to arrange and blend the letter sounds to form the names of the parts of plants. E.g. /r//oo//t, /s//t//e//m, /l//ea//f. Have them spell and pronounce the words using "Pick and spell". Have learners make simple sentences with the words and then fill in the missing letters in the given words into their exercise books. Have discuss 2-D and 3-D objects using real and drawn objects. Have them compare some of the objects according to a given attributes as done in K1.6.5.1.2.

indicators.description: Use a variety of new vocabulary learnt about plants to make simple sentences, draw and write the initial letter sounds.

exemplars.description: Using a clearly labelled tree, recap lessons on the parts of tree and take learners through the keywords, guide them to identify the initial letter sounds. Have learners play "Show and tell" or "Letter hunt" to highlight the initial sound of the words. Ask learners to draw and indicate the initial letter sounds of the parts.

indicators.description: Make art works with the elements of art

exemplars.description: Using leaves and saw dust, guide learners to make a collage of a tree and talk about their art work indicating the parts of a plant. Using positive language, have learners make simple sentence about their art work.

indicators.description: Describing the position and motion of objects in relation to others.

exemplars.description: Recap lessons of position of objects. Using pictures of different kinds of plants, guide learners to identify and talk about the position of each of the plants. E.g. The flower is the 5th. Ask learners to colour a particular position. Extend the activities to include number/object grid.

subStrands.title: Plants - 2
subStrands.description: Understanding plant growth, needs, and classification.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of how plants grow

indicators.description: Talk about and discuss how plants and what human should do to enhance the growth process

exemplars.description: Have learners sit in a semi-circle position and recite a rhyme about plants. E.g. "Plants can grow". Have learners identify the key things said about plants in the rhyme. Using pictures, discuss with learners how plants grow; emphasizing on the things plants need in order to grow well (water, air, good soil). Have learners use the treated keywords form sentences on how plants grow. Using LEA, have learners compose simple story on a manila card about how plant grow. Have learners illustrate their composed story.

indicators.description: Talk about the cover page and identify how plants grow in a read aloud story

exemplars.description: Using a story book on the theme, ask learners to talk about the cover page and open the book correctly. Have learners do pretend reading and guide them open the pages correctly. Using Echo-reading strategy, read aloud the story and guide learners to read aloud too. Use questions to assist learners to monitor their understanding and highlight the proper handling of books. Use varied questions for the after-reading stage to reinforce the proper handling of books. Ask simple questions about the story for learners to answer. Provide learners with different drawn and real objects like tins of milk, milo, etc. empty boxes of sugar, etc. kites etc. and have them discuss according to a given attributes. Have them discuss 2-D and 3-D objects using real and drawn objects and compare some of the objects according to a given attributes as done in K1.6.5.1.2. Have learners colour outline of cut out shapes.

indicators.description: Identify the initial and ending letter sounds of objects and blend letter sounds to form words.

exemplars.description: Have learners talk about pictures and the beginning and ending sounds of their labels. Drill learners on the initial and ending sounds of words which relates to the theme. E.g. plant -beginning letter sound /p/, stem /s/ etc. Ending sounds for Plant and stem are /t/, /m/. Extend the activity to include other words enhance learners understanding. Using the letter cards, guide learners to arrange letter cards and decode words which relates to the topic. Learners write selected words and show their beginning and ending sounds in their books e.g. root, leaf, roots, etc.

indicators.description: Use vocabulary learnt to form simple meaningful sentences

exemplars.description: Using pictures and word cards, guide learners to read the words. Use short stories and illustrations to help learners understand the selected words/keyword. Guide learners to use the keywords acquired to construct simple sentences about the theme. E.g. We need plant for shade; plants need water to grow well; Plants can be used for medicine; Plants can be used for food; etc. Using the provided 2-D and 3-D objects and drawn objects, have learners describe the characteristics of the everyday objects and shapes in their environment. Have them match objects that look alike in terms of shapes. Have learners draw and colour any object in 2-D and compare their drawing using positive language.

indicators.description: Identify, observe and talk about art in the immediate

exemplars.description: Using conversational poster/pictures, have learners talk about uses of plants e.g. for shade, food, medicine, etc. Have learners repeat this activity by discussing the shapes of the objects on the poster in terms of 2-D and 3-D (e.g. roof of a building-2-D/3-D, building-2-D/3-D, etc. items in a store-2-D/3-D). Extend this activity with a conversational poster on fruit and vegetables and ask learners to observe and talk about the art work. Have learner make their own picture about fruits and vegetables and compare them using positive language.

indicators.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category up to 9.

exemplars.description: Using pictures of fruits and vegetable, guide learners to sort, group and count the fruit and match with a numeral card.

subStrands.title: Gardening
subStrands.description: Understanding soil types and their use in gardening.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the types of soil.

indicators.description: Talk about different types of soil and which one is best used for gardening.

exemplars.description: In a community circle time, learners recite a poem about gardening "I have my garden". Have learners observe and talk about a conversational poster on the different types of soil. E.g. sandy, clayey and loamy soil. Using different types of soil in separate containers, have learners watch and feel the types of soil (make sure learners wash their hands well after this activity). Discuss with learners how to make soil fertile for a successful gardening. You can guide learners plant seed in the three types of soil and observe them daily for a class project (Let them water them daily).

indicators.description: Point to individual words to track reading.

exemplars.description: In the community circle time learner sit in a horse shoe form with the help of the big book, ask learners to identify the cover page and talk briefly about the colours and pictures. Guide them point to the title of the book. Have them point to the individual words in the title. Guide them to use the cover page picture to predict the content. Using Echo-reading, read aloud the sentences as you point to the individual words while reading. Show pictures for learners to make predictions to monitor understanding. At the post-reading stage, have learners tell part they liked most in the reading and why they say so. Have learners use some of the gardening words to make simple sentences. Have learners colour outlines of some of the farm tools mentioned in the reading and talk about their colouring using positive language. Have learners sort and group the farm tools according to colours and use comparative language ("more than", "less than" "same as") to compare their art work. Extend the activity to include addition and subtraction.

indicators.description: Use a variety of new vocabulary learnt about soil to make simple sentences about it.

exemplars.description: Using word card game, teacher places word cards upside down in front of learners. In turns, learners pick cards for teacher to read. Learners repeat the word. Asks learners to form own sentence with the word (e.g. I play in the sand. Some trees are tall). Write some of the sentences on the board for them. Using conversational poster, have learners through LEA compose a simple story on the pictures using some of the keywords on the word cards (Write their story on manila card). Guide them to illustrate their story. With the use of conversational poster, have learners identify the following: people, farm tools, buildings, and trees. Have learner represent them with counters (bottle tops, sticks, shells, etc) and count the number in each group. Let learners use comparative language to describe the groups. You can extend this to include addition and subtraction.

indicators.description: Recognise and create words with given sounds and make art works with the elements of art

exemplars.description: Have learners sing a song or recite a rhyme/poem on farm/garden. With selected words from the song/rhyme/poem, have learner tell the common sound in the words e.g. soil, toil, coil, boil etc. Have learners mention a words on word cards after you and identify the common sound e.g. rake, make, take, fake, etc. Guide learners to use given sounds to form the words using the letter cards. E.g. -in: /t//i//n/ (tin), p///i//n/ (pin), /b//i//n/ (bin), /s//i//n/ (sin), etc. -oil: /s//oi//l/ (soil), /f//o//i//l/ (foil), etc. -arm: /f//a//r//m/ (farm), /b//a//r//m/ (barm), /s//w//a//r//m/ (swarm). Have learners use clay to mould objects e.g. farm tool and paint once it is dry and discuss their art works using positive language. Representing art works with counters, have learners sort and group their art works according to colour and/or size. Have learners count the number in each group. You can extend the activity with addition, subtraction, or comparison activities.

indicators.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category up to 9

exemplars.description: Read a concept book (if you do not have numbers concept book, create one) on numbers (1-9) to learners. Let learners talk about the numbers heard in the reading and show their respective cut out number. Give learners variety of objects (bottle tops, straws, sticks) ask learners to pick cut out number and count e.g. straws that matches with the particular number on the card.

subStrands.title: Light - Day and Night
subStrands.description: Exploring natural and man-made sources of light.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the sources of light for day and night.

indicators.description: Recite rhymes/poems and talk about the different sources of light.

exemplars.description: In a community circle time, teachers lead learners recite the rhyme (twinkle, twinkle little star……) Have the pictures of the keywords in the rhyme on cards and assist learners to talk about them. Through questions, lead learners to talk about the source of light displayed on a conversational poster. E.g. what gives us light during the day to see the faces of our friends? When do we see the stars? What else do we see up the sky at night? Have learners share their experiences with the natural lights. Have learners draw any of the natural sources of light they like and talk about their art work.

indicators.description: Use pictures and other text features to aid understanding as they listen to a read aloud informational text on sources light.

exemplars.description: Have learners discuss the cover page of the Big book at the pre-reading stage. Through picture walk, have them predict the content of the text. As you read aloud the book with the learners, point to the words to enable track the reading on sources of light. Ask questions while reading at vantage point to assist you monitor learners' understanding the content of the book. At the post-reading stage, ask questions enable learners use pictures to retell the story. Have learners mention the sources of light read about and group them according to daylights (e.g. sun, electricity) and nightlights (moon, stars, electricity, candles, lanterns etc.). Assist learners to make sentences with the examples of sources of lights. Have learners group the examples of lights talked about and count the number in each group. Have them do addition and subtraction activities with the examples of lights. Include word problem in these activities. Have them draw and colour any example of man-made light read about label it.

indicators.description: Recognise the beginning sound of the letters in relation to the types of light and write in their books.

exemplars.description: Using a conversational poster and letter cards, guide learners to identify and name the sources of light. Mention one source and ask learners to identify the initial, middle and ending sound. E. g. Initial Sound Middle Sound Ending sound. Moon /m/ /oo/ /n/. Sun /s/ /u/ /n/. Stars /st/ /ar/ /s/. Light /l/ /igh/-/ai/ /t/. Provide learners with letters card and ask them to pick the letter card that represent the initial letter of the word you mention. Let them use this activity to identify the middle and ending sounds of selected words. Let them repeat this activity in small groups. Assist learners to arrange letter cards to form a given source of light. Have them draw any of the sources of light and write the initial and ending sounds of the name and use positive language to talk about their art work.

indicators.description: Use a variety of new vocabulary learnt about light to form sentences orally.

exemplars.description: In a community circle time, have learners talk about the different uses of the sources of light on a conversations poster. Have learners discuss the uses of light in their everyday life using the new vocabulary learnt. Have learners pick a word card and make simple sentence with it. E.g. Switch the torch light on; put the candle off; etc. Guide them pick and act out simple sentences on sentence strips in relation to the theme E.g. Switch on the light, switch off the torch, light the lantern, etc. You can let learners do charade activity with the sentence strips in pairs. Have learners do addition and subtraction activities with the examples of lights using simple everyday situation word problem e.g. Kofi was sent to buy 5 bulbs from a nearby shop. On his way back, he trips and the bag containing the bulbs fell and one got broken, how many bulbs would the family use?

indicators.description: Identify, observe and talk about art in the immediate natural and manmade environment.

exemplars.description: Using a conversational poster of the sources of light depicting day and night, guide learners to identify the natural and artificial sources. Have learners describe the beauty of the day and night scenes. Have learners connect the lights on the posters to those found in their environment focusing on natural and manmade lights. Guide learners group and count the sources of light in each group and compare them using comparative language. Extend this activity to include additions and subtractions.

indicators.description: Use number names, counting sequences and how to count to find out "how many"? (up to 9)

exemplars.description: Give learners a number of counting objects, recap lessons on counting and sequencing. Using cut out number name cards, assist learners to pick a number name card and count the number using given counters. Let them be in pairs and play "pick and count" (one person picks and the other counts). Let them do this activity individually where learners pick a numeral card and then quickly count objects to match the numeral card. Extend this activity to matching objects with the number name. Do interactive reading on a concept book on number names (if you do not number name create one), and let learner interact actively linking number names with respective numbers. Let learners play with number name cards during the reading and the post-reading stages to enhance their understanding.

subStrands.title: Changing Weather Conditions
subStrands.description: Observations of weather patterns and seasons.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of changing weather conditions and seasons.

indicators.description: Sing and talk about the weather condition in Ghana.

exemplars.description: Have learners sing the "Rain rain go away song" and talk about the weather condition they sang about in the song. Use leading question to introduce the sub-theme to learners. Go out of the classroom to observe the weather with learners. Lead learners to recite a poem on the weather e.g. "Whether the weather..." Using conversational poster on different weather conditions in Ghana, guide learners e.g. rainy, sunny, windy, cloudy, etc. Have learners sound out the names of the weather condition and share personal experiences on weather conditions. Guide them to talk about the current weather condition. E.g. Sunny or cloudy weather. Using a weather tally chart, guide learners to tally the weather for the week as a class project using different colours for different weather conditions. Using a weather chart, discuss with learners how to cater for oneself during the different seasons. Have learners be in pair and do charade depict what they do on different weather conditions.

indicators.description: Identify the cover page and illustrations and listen to and respond to a read aloud text on changes in the weather condition.

exemplars.description: In a community circle time, show the book and ask learners to identify the cover page, the writer/author and the illustrator. Have learners use the cover page illustration and picture walk to predict the content. Using Echo-reading, assist learners to read aloud the text. Ask questions during the reading to help you monitor their understanding. Use different questions (literal, leading, inference, critical) to guide learners respond to the text. Have learners charade with selected sentences in the text e.g. It is raining so I am cold; it is sunny today; etc. Have learners identify the weather conditions read about and tell the order in which they appeared. E.g. rainy weather came 1st, sunny 2nd, windy 3rd, etc. Have them tell the position of the following: table, chair, duster, ruler, chalk (1st to 7th). Extend this numeracy concept with grids for them to describe the position of a given numbers/ object/ etc.

indicators.description: Identify initial letter-sounds of weather and write them under the appropriate pictures.

exemplars.description: Using pictures, guide learners to identify and name the initial letter sounds of the various weather conditions as done in K1.6.8.1.3. Ask learners to use letter cards and match with the pictures. Guide learners to write the letter sounds under picture of the weather conditions. You can let them post the letter under the picture too.

indicators.description: Use the vocabulary learnt to talk about the weather

exemplars.description: Discuss the different weather conditions on a conversational poster with learners. Show keywords on cards and guide learners to read e.g. rainy, windy, sunny, cloudy, rain, wind, etc. Ask them to form sentences orally with the vocabulary acquired. Put learners into groups. Give each group picture word cards of names of the weather - rainy, windy, sunny, cloudy, rain, wind, sun, cloud. In turns learners pick and read out a card and say one thing about the word. Make a chart from the words they read. Have learners draw and colour any of the weather conditions and talk about it.

indicators.description: Identify, observe and talk about art in the immediate

exemplars.description: Using the pictures of the weather, let learners talk about the beauty of each of them. Assist them use the weather vocabulary to make simple sentences (You can make some of these sentences on strips). Have Learners make their own pictures and talk about them. Give out some numeral cards, let learners compare the numbers by using the comparative language "more than", "less than", "same as". Let learners compare the number of objects in the class room. E.g. the pencils are more than the erasers.

strands.title: MY GLOBAL COMMUNITY
strands.description: Learners explore transportation, communication, and trade as ways of connecting with the wider world.

subStrands.title: Connecting and Communicating with the Global Community

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of different ways we connect and communicate with the global world.

indicators.description: Using pictures, talk about the various means by which we connect with the international community-Transportation.

exemplars.description: Recite poem on transport. Discuss means (air, sea, road). Group by choice. Count and compare.

indicators.description: Talk about the various means by which we connect with the international community-Trade

exemplars.description: Discuss buying and selling abroad. Role play trade. LEA story on trade.

indicators.description: Identify and cover and back page of a book and read aloud a simple sentence.

exemplars.description: Identify book parts. Predict content. Echo-reading. Group objects in illustrations.

indicators.description: Blend individual sounds to decode words which relates to the theme and write the words in their books.

exemplars.description: Revise letter sounds. Arrange letters to form words. Make sentences. Draw transport.

indicators.description: Use vocabulary leant to form simple sentences in real life situation.

exemplars.description: Read keywords. Form sentences (e.g. travel to Dubai). Role play buying/selling with money.
